name: Coonawarra

climate: Cabernet Sauvignon, Shiraz and Merlot sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

terms: Australia's Geographical Indications nest in three levels: zones, the regions inside them, and subregions inside those.
keyfacts: Coonawarra, in the Limestone Coast zone of South Australia, is known for Cabernet Sauvignon grown on its terra rossa soil.
The terra rossa strip runs north to south for about 17 miles and is about 1.1 miles wide, over a ridge of free-draining limestone.
West of the ridge, heavy black rendzina clays hold more water and are harder to manage in wet, cool seasons, while a transitional brown rendzina also grows vines successfully.
The climate is maritime influenced, with about 9 inches of rain in the October to April growing season out of about 23 inches a year.
Consistent cloud cover helps keep temperatures down, and the mean January temperature is about 69°F.
Shiraz was the main grape until the 1950s, and the region also makes white wines including Chardonnay and Riesling.

notes: Coonawarra is synonymous with Cabernet Sauvignon, full of plum and blackcurrant fruit.
Its Cabernets brought Australia international attention in the 1970s for intense fruit and subtle mint.

blurb.text: A South Australian region in the Limestone Coast, about 240 miles southeast of Adelaide, known for Cabernet Sauvignon grown on its terra rossa soil. Cabernet Sauvignon is 64 percent of plantings, with Shiraz at 20 percent.
